title: Caritas
hook: the Church's charity agencies carry the word caritas, love, to the ends of the earth

segments.voice: Yesterday, nonviolence, and Paul's line about overcoming evil with good. Your line was active nonviolence. Which conflict got the gentler reply? Day one thousand three hundred twenty-three.

A flood comes through a town, and a few days later a truck pulls up with water, blankets and people in vests. A refugee family lands in a strange city, and someone meets them with a key to an apartment. A man leaves prison with nowhere to go, and a desk somewhere has his name on a list. Look at the logo on the vest or the door, and often enough it says Caritas, or Catholic Charities, or Catholic Relief Services. One Latin word sits behind all of them. Today's word.
screen: `A FLOOD, A TRUCK, A BLANKET.` → `A KEY FOR A NEW FAMILY.` → `ONE LATIN WORD.`

segments.voice: First, the word. Caritas is the Latin the Church uses for love, the self-giving kind. In older English Bibles it comes through as charity, and Paul, writing to the Corinthians, describes it in the Douay-Rheims: "Charity is patient, is kind." So charity, in its first sense, isn't a donation. It's a way of loving. Second, a decision in Acts. The first Christians in Jerusalem share food with widows every day, and a complaint goes up: some widows are being missed. The apostles don't shrug, and they don't drop everything else. They choose seven men to take charge of the daily serving, so the work is done well and no one is skipped. Pope Benedict the Sixteenth, in his letter God is Love, points to that moment. From then on, he says, serving the poor is organized, and it's part of who the Church is. Third, Benedict's big claim. He names three things the Church can't do without: proclaiming the word, celebrating the sacraments, and the service of charity. Take any one away and something essential is missing. Charity isn't an extra the Church does when it has spare time. Fourth, what that grew into. Some parishes run food pantries. Dioceses run charities. Catholic agencies work across borders, joined in a confederation called Caritas Internationalis. Benedict adds one warning: the people who serve need hearts formed by love, not just training, so that a person in need meets a person, not a process. A blanket handed over coldly is still a blanket. Handed over with love, it's caritas.
screen: `CARITAS: LOVE THAT GIVES ITSELF.` · `SEVEN CHOSEN TO SERVE TABLES.` · `WORD, SACRAMENT, CHARITY.` · `A PERSON, NOT A PROCESS.` · then, large: `CHARITY IS PATIENT, IS KIND.`

segments.voice: Here's the practice: give to a charity. Before the sit, if you're able, choose one group that serves people in need, near you or far away, and give something: money, an hour, a bag of clothes, a sign-up for later. Any size counts. Then settle, and breathe. Bring to mind one person that gift might reach. You'll never meet them. Hold them anyway, for a few breaths. If you pray, you can offer the gift and the person to God. The bell holds the time.

Caritas. Latin for the love that gives itself. And this week's road: social friendship, four verbs, people before machines, no one for sale, meant for all, active nonviolence, and now charity everywhere. Today's word.

Your line: charity everywhere. Today, when you see a charity's name on a van, a box or a door, say the word caritas to yourself and remember what it means. Day one thousand three hundred twenty-three.

howItsDone: Catholics give to charity through parish collections, diocesan appeals and agencies such as Caritas, Catholic Charities and Catholic Relief Services, and some parishes run food pantries and volunteer programs of their own.

fork.setup: you're an apostle in Jerusalem. some widows are being missed at the daily serving, and you're already stretched thin. what do you do?
options: stop preaching and serve the tables yourselves.
choose seven people to take charge of the serving.
fork.reveal: they choose seven men for the work, so no one is skipped and the preaching goes on. Benedict XVI points to this as charity becoming organized.

original.note: Latin: love, the self-giving kind, rendered charity in older English Bibles.

what it means: the Latin word for self-giving love, which the Church's charities carry as a name.
what a scholar hears: Deus caritas est, God is love, from 1 John 4, and Benedict XVI's teaching that charity stands beside word and sacrament in the Church's nature.

notes: The index hook says the agencies serve 'in nearly every country'; under the claims rule no count or reach is stated. Script hook reworded; index hook kept in meta.

Deus Caritas Est is paraphrased: §21 on the seven of Acts 6 as the start of organized diakonia; §25 on the threefold responsibility (kerygma-martyria, leitourgia, diakonia); §31 on 'formation of the heart'. Confirm.
Acts 6 does not say 'men' in every translation's phrasing; the Douay has 'seven men of good reputation'. Confirm.
'In older English Bibles it comes through as charity' refers to the Douay-Rheims and KJV rendering of agape/caritas in passages like 1 John 4:8 and 1 Corinthians 13. Confirm phrasing.
